  <div class="masthead">THE EMPTY ROAD</div>
  <nav><a href="#read">Read</a></nav>
</header>

<section class="hero">
  <div class="hero-photo"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="A car parked on an open road as dusk settles over distant hills"></div>
  <div class="hero-content">
    <h1>Why We Still Love To Drive</h1>
    <p class="dek">Every year, cars get better at driving themselves. And every year, people still choose to drive them anyway — not because it's faster, but because of what happens in the hour they spend doing it.</p>
  </div>
</section>

<div id="read" class="rest">
  <article>
    <p class="lede">There's a specific kind of silence that only exists inside a moving car, alone, somewhere past the edge of a city. No phone worth checking. No one asking anything of you. Just a road, a set of headlights, and enough forward motion to make thinking feel <em>easier</em> instead of harder. It's a strange thing to miss about a machine — but people do.</p>
  </article>
</div>

<div class="break-photo reveal">
  <img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="A car's silhouette lit by a single line of light against total darkness">
  <div class="cap">Somewhere between headlights and horizon</div>
</div>

<div class="reading-block reveal">
  <h2>The One Place Nobody Can Reach You</h2>
  <p>Almost everywhere else in a day, someone can find you. A car is one of the last spaces where that isn't quite true — where being unreachable for twenty minutes is simply the cost of getting somewhere, and nobody thinks to question it.</p>
  <p>That's a small kind of freedom, but it adds up. A commute becomes the only part of the day with no one else's agenda attached to it. A late-night drive becomes the only hour built entirely around your own thoughts, with nothing else competing for the space.</p>
</div>

<div class="quote-wrap reveal">
  <div class="bg-photo"><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="A lone van on a long empty road leading toward distant mountains"></div>
  <div class="content">
    <h2>A car doesn't just take you somewhere. For a while, it's the only place you actually have to yourself.</h2>
    <div class="who">On Driving As Solitude</div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="reading-block reveal">
  <h2>Control, In A World That Rarely Offers It</h2>
  <p>Most of a day is spent reacting — to messages, to meetings, to other people's timing. Behind a wheel, that flips. You choose the speed, the route, the moment you slow down or press on. It's a small, mechanical kind of control, but it's yours completely, in a way surprisingly little else in daily life is.</p>
  <p>Maybe that's why the appeal of driving hasn't faded, even as the case for not doing it keeps getting stronger. It was never really about getting somewhere faster. It was about the one stretch of the day where the decisions, however small, are entirely your own.</p>
</div>

<div class="break-photo reveal">
  <img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="A car parked in a dim garage, lit only by its own headlights">
  <div class="cap">Some cars are kept, not just driven</div>
</div>

<div class="closing reveal">
  <h2>Not Every Machine Needs To Be Necessary</h2>
  <p>Self-driving cars will keep getting better. Public transit will keep expanding into places it hasn't reached yet. Neither of those things is really an argument against driving — because driving was never purely about logistics for most of the people who love it.</p>
  <p>It's about a stretch of road, a set of choices only you're making, and a silence that's hard to find anywhere else. That's not something a more efficient alternative can replace. It's just a different thing entirely — and maybe that's exactly why it isn't going anywhere.</p>
</div>

</div>

    entries.forEach(e=>{
      if(e.isIntersecting){
        e.target.classList.add('in');
        io.unobserve(e.target);
      }
    });
  },{threshold:0.15});
  revealEls.forEach(el=>io.observe(el));
